conceptZh: 島是四面被海水圍住的一小塊陸地
object: a chunky toy fire engine with a stubborn rubbery hose and a tiny crew
morph: the hose keeps squirting a blue puddle sea around the glyph 島 until it stands alone like an island
creativeAngle: 消防小隊的水管不聽話，亂噴出一圈海水把字圍成小島；水管打結的反轉讓道具反抗的笑點成立，詞用「小島」。
promptEn: An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale sand-colored backdrop with a locked camera. The only text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 島, centered in saturated ocean-blue strokes, filling about 70 percent of the frame height: the bird-like 鳥 shape on top with its dotted bottom row, resting on the mountain 山 at the base. Cast: a squat red toy fire engine named Dot with a round yellow ladder and big headlight eyes, plus its fat orange rubber hose that has a mind of its own. Moment one, 0 to 1.7s: Dot rolls in from the left, unreels the hose toward the glyph's foot, and the hose wriggles away like a snake, squirting a thin fan of blue water that curls into a pool under the character. The first 島 is spoken as the pool appears. Moment two, 1.7 to 3.4s: Dot grabs the hose nozzle in its tiny clamp and the hose bites back, tying itself into a big knot, so Dot gets squirted in the face with a harmless splash, headlights blinking in surprise. The second 島 is spoken as the strokes pop upright on the water. Moment three, 3.4 to 5.0s: Dot rolls backward in a circle, the knotted hose unspools into a spiral and sprays a perfect ring of rippling water that circles the glyph, leaving a small round beach of pale sand beneath the 山 so the glyph sits alone surrounded by sea. A tiny white paper boat bobs by. Moment four, 5.0s onward: Dot, drenched and proud, parks at the far bottom edge and honks a silent happy bounce on its suspension. From 5.0 to 8.0s the glyph is perfectly still with its ring of water gently shimmering far below the strokes, while Dot's ladder waggles in a happy little wave and the hose gives a tiny salute without touching the character. Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「島、島、小島」, slowly and distinctly with clear tones, as ㄉㄠˇ、ㄉㄠˇ、ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄉㄠˇ. First 島 near 0.8s, second near 2.4s, and 小島 around 5.3s while a tiny paper boat circles the ring. Stop after the word. Only soft splashing, no background music. Soft studio lighting, vivid not neon, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 島.

conceptZh: 調皮小老鼠坐上彈射蹺蹺板想飛去搶小島上的起司，拉布拉多警長衝來阻止卻滑過頭一腳踩中板尾，老鼠被彈飛越過小島撞上一疊藍色積木，積木嘩啦落下排成「島」字，老鼠倒栽進水桶裡，水桶漂成一座迷你小島。
object: a seesaw catapult, a tin bucket floating on a strip of blue water, and a tall stack of ocean-blue toy planks on a small sand mound
morph: the launched mouse BONKs into the plank stack; the planks tumble and settle as the bird-shaped 鳥 top (no four dots) and the 山 nested at its base, forming 島
creativeAngle: 改用「彈射」笑點：老鼠想要的目標（小島上的起司）、警長衝過頭誤踩蹺蹺板、飛越過頭撞倒積木堆，三步都是看得見的肢體動作，撞擊本身讓積木落成「島」。同時修正前一版的錯誤結構描述：島的下方是「山」，不是鳥的四點。「小島」一詞由水桶漂成一座迷你小島具體呈現。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D toy-style animated clip on a clean, solid pale cream backdrop, locked camera, soft bright studio light. A shallow strip of bright blue water runs along the bottom edge. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 島, which will stand centered in thick saturated ocean-blue strokes filling about 70 percent of frame height with clear margins: the bird-shaped 鳥 component on top and, in place of the bird's four bottom dots, the mountain 山 tucked into its base. No other writing anywhere.

Lead: Pip, a tiny cheeky cartoon mouse with huge round ears, a pink nose and a permanent grin. Supporting: Sheriff Biscuit, a big friendly cartoon Labrador with a gold star badge and a whistle.

0 to 1.5s: Bottom-left, Pip sits on the spoon of a toy seesaw catapult, pointing dramatically across the water at a small sand island mid-right that holds one wedge of cheese. Pip rubs its paws, then strikes a drumroll pose, tapping its tail on the plank. Behind the island stands a tall tidy stack of ocean-blue toy planks.

1.5 to 3s: Sheriff Biscuit charges in from the left blowing a silent whistle, trying to stop the launch, skids straight past Pip on the smooth floor, and his big back paw stomps the high end of the seesaw. WHUMP. Pip is flung upward in a huge slow arc, ears flapping, still grinning.

3 to 4.5s: Pip sails clear over the island and the cheese, reaching out and missing by a whisker, and BONKS face-first into the blue plank stack with cartoon squash-and-stretch. The stack explodes outward in a tumble while Pip ricochets backward and plops upside-down into a tin bucket bobbing on the water at bottom-right, only its feet sticking out and kicking.

4.5 to 5s: The scattered planks drop, slide and click into place in the center of the frame, forming the glyph 島 cleanly: the 鳥 shape stacks up first, then the 山 wedges into its base with a satisfying clunk.

5 to 8s: The glyph stays perfectly still and readable. The bucket drifts into the center of the water strip and a little ring of sand rises around it with one tiny palm leaf, turning it into a miniature island. Pip flips right side up inside the bucket, dizzy, wobbles, then holds the cheese wedge up in triumph. Sheriff Biscuit sits at bottom-left wagging his tail, saluting. Nobody touches the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「島、島、小島」 (ㄉㄠˇ、ㄉㄠˇ、ㄒㄧㄠˇ ㄉㄠˇ), reading exactly those syllables slowly and distinctly with clear tones. First 島 near 0.8s as Pip points at the island; second 島 near 4.7s as the planks snap into the glyph; 小島 near 5.8s as the bucket becomes a tiny island with its palm leaf. Stop after the word; no more speech. Only soft boings, a cartoon bonk and gentle splashes, no music louder than the voice. Vivid but not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no text other than the single glyph 島.
